title: Priming cadence cookbook (microcadence & warmup recipes)
content:
Notes to self — working cookbook for small-batch canary priming and version pin behavior. Purpose: capture a repeatable microcadence that ops + SDK teams can use for low-risk flips. This is intentionally concise, tactical, and contains heuristics not policies.

TOPLINE GOAL
- Reduce noisy failures from cold KV/cache-miss behaviour and model-variant friction during tiny canaries (0.1%–2%) by using short, deterministic priming windows and explicit pin/unpin steps.

ASSUMPTIONS / CONTEXT
- Target workload: low- to medium-concurrency chat queries with varied context lengths (~64–512 tokens).
- Serving runtime supports prefix KV caching and sticky client routing for pinned cohorts.
- We have per-tenant telemetry to measure latency P50/P95, error-rate, and quality regression through eval hooks.
- This cookbook is for warmups when flipping model variants or quantization profiles. Not for major schema changes.

PRIMITIVE: microcadence (naming)
- primer: a short, controlled traffic feed that exercises model hot paths for a cohort (duration 3–10m).
- drip: incremental percentage increase after a successful primer (e.g., 0.25% -> 0.5% -> 1%).
- soak: extended low-variance period where telemetry is monitored (30–120m).
- anchor: pinned cohort that remains on old variant to compare relative metrics.

COHORTS (example percentages)
- sneak (primer cohort): 0.05% clients for 5m — synthetic + real small fraction.
- ember (first drip): 0.25% for 10m.
- kindle (second drip): 1% for 30m.
- blaze (general availability ramp): >5% with autoscale checks.
- anchor (control): 1–2% pinned to baseline model for variance comparison.

WARMUP RECIPE (step-by-step)
1) Preflight (10–30m before primer)
   - Verify infra: node counts, memory headroom, GPU temps within normal, KV cache warmed by prior runs.
   - Confirm linked artifacts: RLSD ticket with rollout notes, deploy PR merged, and rollout config present in console.
   - Sanity check: sample inference locally with representative prompts (5–10 samples).

2) Primer (5–10m) - synthetic + real-mix
   - Kick off synthetic warmups that mimic common prompt shapes (prefix-heavy, long-context). Use replay harness or synthetic driver.
   - Open a sneak cohort: route 0.05% real traffic + synthetic steady stream.
   - Observe: initial latency P50/P95, token error types, memory GC patterns.

3) Quick post-primer decision (5m)
   - If P95 regresses >30% over baseline OR error-rate >0.5% absolute increase: abort and rollback.
   - If minor latency increase (<20% P95) with no error uptick, proceed to ember.

4) Ember drip (10m)
   - Increase to 0.25% real traffic. Continue synthetic background warmers at 2x request-rate.
   - Validate: cost-per-token delta, per-route token counts, and KV cache hit-rate.

5) Soak & evaluate (30–120m)
   - Hold kindle/ember level for 30–120m based on variance. Collect metrics: P50/P95, tail latency, errors, model output quality (eval hooks).
   - Run A/B diff vs anchor for quality metrics (automated eval suites if available).

6) Full ramp (if soak good)
   - Move to 1% -> 5% -> 10% in 30–60m steps with health checks at each step.

PINNING AND UNPINNING NOTES
- Pin when: enforcing a stable client experience for a paying tenant, or when doing a canary that should not be impacted by autoscaling moves.
- Unpin procedure: notify client, drain pinned requests, perform canary primer on a mirrored cohort, then unpin once soak is good.
- Pin fallback: keep an anchor cohort pinned at ~1% for the entire rollout for continuous relative comparison.

OBSERVABILITY CHECKLIST (must-have signals)
- Latency: P50/P90/P95/P99 per-cohort and per-route.
- Errors: 400/500 breakdown, model inference exceptions, truncated responses.
- Resource: GPU utilization, memory headroom, host CPU.
- Quality: automated eval pass-rate on representative prompt set (perf delta threshold), hallucination spike detector.
- Cache metrics: KV cache hit-rate, cache eviction pressure.
- Business signals: key tenant success metrics if available (conversion, engagement) as an optional high-signal fallback.

ESCALATION TRIGGERS (fast path)
- Immediate rollback: 1) sustained P95 > 2x baseline for 10m, 2) error rate >1% absolute increase sustained 5m, 3) automated eval regression >5% on guard prompts.
- Soft hold: minor regressions (P95 up 20–50% OR eval regression 1–5%): pause ramp and increase primer soak to 2x.

FAILURE MODES & QUICK MITIGATIONS
- Cold-cache storm: synthetic warmers at 3x until KV hit-rate stabilizes; if persistent, revert to prior quant/profile.
- Model numeric instability: reduce max decode length, enable temperature clamp, or pin back immediately.
- Autoscaler thrash: temporarily cap burst concurrency for new cohort or route traffic to dedicated capacity.

EXAMPLE CLI / SDK STEPS (ops cheats)
- create cohort: rctl rollout cohort create --name sneak --percent 0.05 --model variant-X --duration 600
- prime with synthetic: rctl traffic synthetic --template short-chat --rps 50 --duration 600 --cohort sneak
- snapshot metrics: rctl metrics snapshot --cohort sneak --out sneak-metrics.json

POST-MORTEM PROMPTS (if any incident)
- What signal changed first? (latency, error, cache)
- Was synthetic warmup representative of real traffic?
- Were any tenant-level pins in place that changed routing?
- Did autoscaler or node drain coincide with regression window?
- Actionables: update primer templates, add guard prompts to eval, change drip timings.

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODO
- Small experiment: compare 5m primer vs 15m primer for long-context models (LL-Medium-1).
- Should we standardize primer synthetic mix per product vertical? (search vs chat vs embed)
- Add a console quick-button to create a sneak cohort + synthetic warmers in one click.

QUICK ACTION ITEMS (me)
- Draft RLSD ticket template for microcadence deployments (T: 30m).
- Add two guard prompts to eval suite for the next flip (T: 1d).
- Pair with Oliver to add synthetic templates for long-context probes (T: 2d).

NOTES TO SELF
- Keep primer small and scripted; the less manual fiddling, the more reproducible the outcome.
- Prefer many short priming windows over one long, uncontrolled ramp when uncertainty is high.

End of draft. This is something I can hand the on-call person to run with minimal context. Save and iterate.
